findings.trigger: Take requirement req-4 'Presented quarterly results to the board for 3+ years' and answer {choice: A_FEW_TIMES, detail: null}. Line 504 makes the text of fact ans-req-4 the requirement text. The summary 'Presented quarterly results to the board for 3+ years' then cites ans-req-4. Check 2 passes, because '3' is in a cited source, and the verifier sees a fact that supports every word. The candidate only said 'a few times', and the choice is not in the fact text. The JD's wording, scope and numbers become a candidate claim. The fix added this fallback. #95 c2 leaves the text open.
findings.title: Fallback fact text makes the JD requirement text a confirmed candidate fact

findings.rule: PLAN 2.3 truth rule; apps-backend #95 c4; contract 4.4 answer rule 4
findings.trigger: Take an answer with detail 'Presented the variance report to the CFO at Infosys' and an Infosys bullet {entryId: INF, sourceIds: [ans-req-4-b1]}. This is the 'Added' Infosys bullet that PLAN 2.3 allows when the detail names the employer. Line 507 says that the `ans-` source 'sits next to at least one source bullet of E', so the server drops the bullet. An entry E with no bullets can never take an answer bullet. Neither PLAN 2.3 nor #95 c4 has this co-citation condition. Rule 4 (line 514) still implies that a named entry gets a new bullet. The phrase 'sits next to' can also be read as position, so the device FabricationGuard (W2-G) and #95 may implement different rules.
findings.title: Answer rule 2 adds a co-citation condition that PLAN 2.3 and #95 lack

findings.trigger: The v2 export lists `unlocks` as {applicationId, creditKind, createdAt}. The v1 contract (e387b855 line 556) and apps-backend main export.ts (lines 38-40, 77-79) return `unlockedAt`. A #89 builder who follows this contract renames an existing export field. The app treats the field as opaque, so nothing breaks today, but the contract and the server disagree.
